variant_decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'not being without law to God' with the same 'to' it uses for 'under law to Christ'; that flat rendering does not distinguish genitive θεοῦ from dative θεῷ.
'under law to Christ' renders ἔννομος Χριστοῦ and ἔννομος Χριστῷ alike; ASV marks no case distinction here.
κερδάνω and κερδήσω are alternative aorist subjunctive forms of the same verb; 'that I might gain' fits either.
'them that are without law' supplies an English relative for ἀνόμους with or without the article τούς; ASV gives no signal of the article.

alignments.note: Article takes the determiner with the dative's case preposition riding along under rule 21.
Substantival adjective, bare behind its own article.
Subjunctive with subject and modal; head on the lexical verb.

The article's complement is a substantival quantifier and no noun is expressed, so the supplied nominal *men* is the article's own under rules 49 and 102, exactly as `οἱ ἡμέτεροι` → *our people* gives *people* to the article; the dative's case preposition rides along as rule 102's `τοῦ κυρίου` → *the kingdom* of has it, and rule 22 heads the unit on the nominal word. Discontinuous around *all* under rule 15.
Substantival quantifier keeps a bare *all*, the supplied nominal having gone to the article that governs it.
Perfect with subject and auxiliary; head on the lexical verb.
Anarthrous substantival quantifier with its generic completion; no article competes, so rule 102's anarthrous clause keeps *things* on the quantifier and rule 17 heads there.
Adverb rendered by the frame *by all means*; head on *all*, the word realizing the παντ- lexeme, rather than on the frame's formal noun (rule 17). Heading on *means* remains defensible.
Subjunctive with subject and modal; head on the lexical verb, discontinuous around the adverbial frame under rule 15.

review_notes: Corrected: `τοῖς` (s009) is `aligned` to *to … men* rather than left `unrepresented`. Rule 21's determinerless clause is for an article governing an expressed noun; here the complement is a substantival quantifier and the ASV supplies the nominal, which rules 49 and 102 make the article's own — `οἱ ἡμέτεροι` → *our people* is the determinerless instance, and rule 102 records the substantival-adjective shape as twelve units to none.
`πᾶσιν` accordingly keeps a bare *all*, matching this chapter's own `τὰ πνευματικά` → *things* / *spiritual* and `τὰ σαρκικά` → *things* / *carnal* at 9:11 (rule 24).
9:19's anarthrous `πάντων` → *all men* is untouched: rule 102 scopes rule 17's generic-noun clause to anarthrous Greek, where no article stands to take the supplied noun.
The head of `πάντως` → *by all means* is contested; the unit's note names the competing reading.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'To the weak I became weak', without the 'as' it uses throughout the surrounding series ('as a Jew', 'as under the law', 'as without law'). The absence of that comparative just where the parallel would invite it answers to the base reading without ὡς.
'I am become all things to all men' renders πάντα with or without the article τά; ASV does not distinguish articular τὰ πάντα from bare πάντα.

alignments.note: Substantival quantifier with generic completion; head on the quantifier under rule 17.
Discontinuous *for … sake* wrap on a proper preposition, headed on the prepositional word under rule 78.
Governed noun, the possessive *'s* being the English idiom of the *for … sake* frame.
`συγκοινωνός` spelled as *joint partaker*: *partaker* glosses the κοινων- root and *joint* the prefix, so rule 66 heads on the noun; the supplied indefinite is a helper.
Subjunctive with subject and modal; head on the verb word.

review_notes: `διά` heads on *for* under rule 78's settled reading for a proper preposition wrapped as *for … sake*.
`συγκοινωνός` heads on *partaker* under rule 66: the English noun glosses the lexeme rather than completing it.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'And I do all things for the gospel's sake' — a plural object, πάντα; r01's Τοῦτο would give the singular 'this I do'.

alignments.note: Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else under rule 32.
Anarthrous noun with supplied indefinite as a helper (ASV margin: Greek *race-course*).
Participle with its relativizer under rule 32.

Correlative `μέν` with no English word written for it; the answering `δέ` keeps its own *but*, so rule 70 leaves this empty. A reference comparison will report it as a disagreement and that is not a correction.
`οὕτως` takes the whole correlative *Even so*, headed on *so* under rule 100.
Subjunctive with subject and modal; head on the lexical verb.

review_notes: `μέν` is `unrepresented` under rule 70, the ASV writing no *indeed* and the answering `δέ` keeping its own *but*.
`οὕτως` keeps *Even so* whole and heads on *so*, per rule 100 and rule 82's refusal to head such a unit on *even*.

alignments.note: Connective δέ realized by the verse-opening And.
Quantifier πᾶς takes every; the ASV writes a second English word (man) for the article, so rule 80's single-word compression does not apply and the ordinary split of rules 22 and 32 holds.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the nominal word and nothing else (rules 22, 32, 80): man is the article's, the relativizer belongs to the participle.

Participle rendered as a finite relative clause: that is a rule 7/31 helper on the participle. The supplied in the games completes the athletic sense of ἀγωνίζομαι itself and no other token licenses it (rules 7, 103), so it rides inside this unit; head on the verb word striveth per rule 17. Marking in the games added remains defensible, but no source token is spent that would license it elsewhere.
Support-verb rendering: exerciseth carries no sense of its own and self control is the meaning-bearing complement, so rule 17 heads on control (as bear witness heads on witness).

Accusative of respect; the supplied in realizes the case and stays with the anarthrous word under rule 21's determinerless clause. Rule 17's generic-noun clause heads a substantival adjective expanded with things on all.

Correlative μέν: the ASV writes no indeed, and marking the correlation elsewhere is not writing it (rule 70). A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.

The Greek clause has no finite main verb; the ASV supplies do it. The expressed subject is a substantival demonstrative, which falls on rule 53's pronoun side under rule 68 and carries the supplied verb itself (cf. τοῦτο … τρίτον → This is now the third time). Folding do it onto λάβωσιν remains defensible, but that verb already has its own English word receive.
Purpose ἵνα realized by the infinitival to that introduces its English clause (rule 40); the verb stands alone.
Subjunctive rendered by the bare infinitive receive, its marker having gone to ἵνα under rule 40.
Attributive adjective takes a bare corruptible; the supplied determiner belongs to the noun under rule 58.
Anarthrous noun takes the supplied indefinite determiner under rules 51 and 58, headed on the noun.
Emphatic nominative pronoun takes we; the clause's verb is elliptical in Greek and the ASV supplies none.
The noun is elliptical, so the adjective is substantival in the English and takes the supplied determiner as an ordinary rule 51 helper on the anarthrous word it determines.

review_notes: s008 μέν is the only unrepresented unit; every other source token and all 27 target tokens are partitioned exactly once.
πᾶς ὁ ἀγωνιζόμενος is split three ways under rules 22, 32 and 80 because the ASV wrote a separate English word for the article (man) rather than compressing the pair into whosoever.

Two judgment calls are recorded in the unit notes: in the games folded onto ἀγωνιζόμενος rather than marked added, and the supplied do it placed on the demonstrative subject under rule 68 rather than on λάβωσιν.

alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject, inverted in the English (ASV margin: Greek *box*); head on the verb word.
Anarthrous noun with supplied determiner as a rule 51 helper.

review_notes: Both `οὕτως` tokens take a bare *so*; no correlative frame is written here, so rule 100 is not in question.
`ἀέρα` is anarthrous, so its *the* is a rule 51 helper on the noun rather than an article's realization.

alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject (ASV margin: Greek *bruise*).
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive *my*.

`δουλαγωγῶ` recast as *bring it into bondage*; rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement, the supplied object being a rule 7 helper.
Negative particle rendered *lest*; the ASV writes a separate phrase for `πως`, so rule 39's single-word cluster does not apply.
Indefinite adverb rendered *by any means*; head on *any*, the word realizing the indefinite, with *means* the generic completion under rule 17.
Dative adjective with its case preposition; no article stands to anchor a determiner.
Participle expanded into a finite clause; the supplied subordinator, subject and auxiliary are its helpers under rule 86 (ASV margin: *have been a herald*).
Privative adjective rendered by the single word *rejected*.
Subjunctive with supplied subject and modal; head on the verb word *be*, discontinuous around *myself* under rule 15.

review_notes: `μή` and `πως` are split rather than joined: the ASV writes *lest* and *by any means* as separate expressions, and rule 39's cluster requires a single English word.
`δουλαγωγῶ` heads on *bondage* under rule 17's resultative clause rather than on the finite *bring*.
